response.sql:
WITH per_timespan AS (
  SELECT
    o.timespan,
    AVG(f.rebrate / f.feerate) AS avg_ratio,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS distinct_order_count
  FROM fees AS f
  JOIN orders AS o
    ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
kept AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM per_timespan
  WHERE distinct_order_count > (
    SELECT AVG(distinct_order_count)
    FROM per_timespan
  )
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_group_avg_ratios,
  SUM(distinct_order_count) AS sum_distinct_order_counts,
  AVG(distinct_order_count - (
    SELECT AVG(distinct_order_count)
    FROM per_timespan
  )) AS avg_excess_count
FROM kept

assumptions.assumption: The ratio is computed per fee row as rebrate / feerate, and SQL AVG ignores rows where either value is NULL; each time-span group is retained even if its ratios are all missing.
